title: Run async work with Tokio
summary: Await a future and join spawned tasks on a Tokio runtime.

scenario.briefing: A telemetry aggregator calls async total functions but never awaits them, so it prints a future instead of a number. Run the work on Tokio, spawn the independent totals, and join their results.

objectives.description: Await an async function and join spawned tasks.
Explain why calling an async function does not run it.
Explain futures, spawning, and blocking accurately.

hints: An async function returns a future until it is awaited.
Annotate main with #[tokio::main] and make it async.
Use tokio::spawn for the independent totals.
Join the handles with tokio::join! and await the local total.

misconceptions.description: Printing a future without awaiting it.
misconceptions.testDescription: The async work is awaited before use.
misconceptions.feedback: Calling an async function only creates a future. Await it or join its handle to obtain the value.

misconceptions.description: Believing calling an async function starts a thread.
misconceptions.feedback: An async call creates a lazy future. The executor schedules it when the future is polled.

misconceptions.description: Blocking a runtime worker with synchronous work.
misconceptions.feedback: Blocking calls prevent the executor from running other tasks on that worker. Use async I/O or move blocking work off the runtime.

sections.title: Futures are lazy
sections.body: Calling an async function returns a future. The future does not run until an executor polls it. await drives one future to completion, and tokio::join! drives several concurrently. A future that is never awaited does no work.

sections.title: The runtime drives tasks
sections.body: Tokio provides the executor and the reactor for I/O. #[tokio::main] turns an async main into a runtime entry point. tokio::spawn schedules a task on the runtime and returns a JoinHandle that must be awaited to observe its result.

sections.title: Keep async work non-blocking
sections.body: Blocking a runtime worker prevents other tasks from making progress. Use async I/O and async synchronization primitives. Values held across an await must be Send when the task is spawned, so avoid holding non-Send guards across suspension points.

[package]
name = "campus-check"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }

tests.description: The program uses the Tokio runtime.
The async work is awaited before use.
Concurrent tasks are spawned and joined.

hints: The current main is synchronous and prints a future.
Add the Tokio main attribute and make main async.
Spawn the independent totals so they run concurrently.
Await one local total and join the two handles.

steps.title: Why nothing happens
steps.prompt: An async function is called but its future is never awaited. Why does no work happen?

options.label: The future is lazy and must be polled by an executor.
Calling an async function starts a thread that exits immediately.
The call panics unless it is inside main.
The call requires an unsafe block.

quiz.explanation: An async function returns a future. Work starts when an executor polls it, which await or a runtime operation such as join! triggers.

hints: An async call returns a value representing future work.

steps.title: Futures and runtime

statements.label: Calling an async function returns a future without running the body.
tokio::spawn schedules a future on the runtime and returns a JoinHandle.
Blocking calls inside async tasks are harmless to the runtime.
A spawned task must hold Send values across await points.

steps.explanation: Futures are lazy, spawn schedules them, and blocking or non-Send state can break a runtime task.
hints: A runtime worker is a shared resource.
Spawned tasks may move between workers.
